text:
Sean Walker has been scoring like a forward lately. The undrafted defenseman, a Stanley Cup winner with Carolina last spring, has four goals in his last ten games: two in Winnipeg on Nov. 1, then goals on back-to-back nights against Edmonton and the Rangers. ESPN's headline on the Edmonton one: "Sean Walker scores from the center ice logo for Carolina."

Our numbers call the run mostly earned. He's getting more chances of his own (1.3 expected goals over the ten games, against 1.0 usual), and 51 shots in 24 games is real volume. But he's shooting 9.8%, above his usual range, with 5 goals on 2.7 expected, and the Hurricanes have scored 5.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

The defending is the reason he plays 21 minutes. Carolina takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a little under its rate without him, and Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.3 wins above replacement last season, 52nd among 215 defensemen, mostly from even-strength defense, while noting that strong teammates flatter his raw numbers. Treat the goals as a bonus and the defending as the job.
